summary: 10 vectorization and state-machine micro-kernels: 5 TSVC loops and 5 CoreMark kernels. Every kept file is a byte-identical copy of the pinned upstream file. Nothing was compiled or executed, and no code was modified.

sources.name: TSVC (adaptation in llvm-test-suite)
sources.retrievalMethod: git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse into an empty scratch directory, then sparse checkout of MultiSource/Benchmarks/TSVC only
sources.originalSource: Maleki et al., An Evaluation of Vectorizing Compilers, PACT 2011, doi 10.1109/PACT.2011.68. The llvm-test-suite README cites http://polaris.cs.uiuc.edu/~maleki1/TSVC.tar.gz as the original download.
sources.adaptationNotes: From the llvm-test-suite README: the iteration count became a command-line parameter, per-type variants were added (the original tests only floats), categories were split into separate directories, and timing was removed from the output.
sources.variantUsed: float (-flt) category directories. The README states the original TSVC tests only floats, so the float variant is the faithful one.
sources.license: Permissive University of Illinois (NCSA-style) license, copyright 2011 University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign and Polaris Research Group. MultiSource/Benchmarks/TSVC/LICENSE.TXT copied to tsvc/LICENSE.TXT. The llvm-test-suite root LICENSE.TXT differs from it and was not copied.

kernels.justification: Simple map X[i] = Y[i] + 1 (tsc.inc:835). Reference case for a fully vectorizable loop.

for (i = 1; i < LEN; i += 2) a[i] = a[i-1] + b[i] (tsc.inc:861-862). Writes hit odd indices and reads hit even indices, so there is no loop-carried dependence. The test is the stride-2 access pattern with a read and a write to the same array, which a dependence test must disambiguate. Chosen as the strided-access case.
if (b[i] > 0) a[i] += b[i] * c[i] (tsc.inc:2799-2800). Conditional store that needs if-conversion or masking to vectorize. Chosen as the conditional case.
sum += a[i] (tsc.inc:3502). Vectorizing a floating-point sum requires reassociation, which strict FP semantics do not allow. Chosen as the reduction case.

a[i] += a[i-1] * b[i] (tsc.inc:4012). First-order linear recurrence: each iteration reads the value the previous iteration wrote, so it cannot be vectorized as written. Chosen as the loop-carried-dependence case.

Workload entry point for the state machine. It runs core_state_transition (core_state.c:217) over the input twice, with byte corruption in between, using data-dependent branches and per-state counters. It is called from calc_func (core_list_join.c:91).

Linked-list workload entry point, called from core_main.c:65 and core_main.c:67 with finder_idx 1 and -1. It performs pointer-chasing core_list_find, core_list_reverse, core_list_remove, core_list_undo_remove, and core_list_mergesort (with two comparators) on list_head nodes.
Matrix workload entry point. It calls matrix_test (core_matrix.c:130), which runs matrix_add_const, matrix_mul_const, matrix_mul_vect, matrix_mul_matrix, matrix_mul_matrix_bitextract, and matrix_sum.

Eight-iteration loop with a data-dependent branch (core_util.c:169-186). crcu16 calls it twice, and crc16 and crcu32 reach it through crcu16, so crcu8 is the only computational CRC kernel in core_util.c.

kernels.behavior: integer strided reduction with bit-field extraction
kernels.justification: Fifth CoreMark kernel. The other matrix kernels in core_bench_matrix are plain multiply and add. This one takes int16 operands (MATDAT_INT, coremark.h:104-107) into int32 products, extracts bit fields with shift-and-mask (bit_extract, core_matrix.c:49), reads B with a column stride of N, and reduces into C[i*N+j]. It is called from matrix_test (core_matrix.c:154). It adds an integer, bit-manipulating vectorization case that the floating-point TSVC loops do not cover.

coremarkPort.reason: The upstream Makefile sets PORT_DIR=macos on Darwin. macos/core_portme.mak includes posix/core_portme.mak, which sets PORT_SRCS = posix/core_portme.c. The simple/ port was not used.

coremarkChecksumCheck.cause: Commit 4ee6eca (2023-10-06, 'Fix typo') changed one comment word in coremark.h (ultithread to multithread) and did not regenerate coremark.md5, which was last updated in 9d07b05 (2022-06-15). At 9d07b05 all six entries match, and no later commit touches the other five files.
coremarkChecksumCheck.option: Re-pinning CoreMark to 9d07b05 would make all six entries match. Not done, because the pinned commit is the current HEAD.

excludedFromUpstream: CoreMark: Makefile, README.md, barebones_porting.md, coremark.md5 (used only for the checksum check above), all *.mak build fragments, and every port tree except posix/ (barebones, simple, linux, macos, cygwin, freebsd, rtems, zephyr, docs).

TSVC: README, all CMakeLists.txt files, all *.reference_output files, the llvm-test-suite root LICENSE.TXT, and the 32 category directories not used (every -dbl variant and the unused -flt categories).
notes: tsc.inc defines every TSVC kernel, and each category tsc.c enables its kernels through the TESTS flag. Building the LinearDependence-flt entry also runs the other LINEAR_DEPENDENCE kernels (s1111, s112, and so on). Downstream builds need a harness-level selection, since no code was edited here.
The CoreMark core_bench_* functions run through iterate() in core_main.c and need the rest of the harness, so they are not standalone programs.

The TSVC license is a permissive University of Illinois (NCSA-style) license. It is not on the approved-license list in the user's dependency-management rules. It governs benchmark source rather than a package dependency, so it is flagged for review.
